lines.text: In World War Two, one of the soldiers in the Polish army was a bear.
In 1942, Polish soldiers in Iran bought an orphaned cub, so small he could barely swallow.
lines.note: Accounts of who sold him differ

lines.text: So they fed him condensed milk, from an old vodka bottle.
He grew up wrestling the soldiers, and his favourite drink became beer.
Then, a problem. The British ships to Italy didn't allow pets.
lines.note: British transport rules banned mascots and pets

lines.text: So the army enlisted him. Private Wojtek. With his own paybook, rank, and serial number.
Then came the Battle of Monte Cassino. His unit says he carried 100 pound crates of artillery shells.
lines.note: Debated · at least one British soldier recalled seeing it

lines.text: And never dropped a single one.
His company made him their badge, and promoted him to corporal.
lines.note: The 22nd Company's emblem: a bear carrying a shell

lines.text: After the war, he retired to Edinburgh Zoo.
Old Polish soldiers came to visit. And when they called to him in Polish, he still answered.
For sixteen years, he was the highest-ranking animal in the zoo.
